method.baseline_diff: Compared dirty integration changes against the specified HEAD; relay_guard previously stopped at the first descriptor predicate and returned seen immediately for an unaccepted descriptor subject.
method.extra_probe: Ran an in-memory (no file changes) relay containing a sink before an accepted descriptor guard and a second sink after it. Detector retained an AUTH-01 finding at Relay::OnRemoteRequestInner for the earlier sink (line 5 in the synthetic source); the later guard did not erase this per-sink candidate.

assessment.wrong_earlier_comparison: Fixed for the reviewed case. analysis.py:1842-1851 continues after a descriptor comparison whose resolved subject is not accepted; analysis.py:1852-1870 credits a later accepted descriptor only if its mismatch branch leaves and a switch follows. The relay fixture test at tests/test_ipc_relay_guard.py:60-61 verifies an earlier IBar comparison no longer masks a later IFoo guard.
assessment.multiple_sinks: T5 matrix covers guard before both dispatches (tests/test_ipc_multidispatch_guard_matrix.py:56-58), between dispatches (60-62), after both (64-65), and wrong-interface check before the later correct guard (67-70). In the between case, expected [0] preserves the pre-guard sink and suppresses the post-guard sink. An additional in-memory combined relay probe confirmed the pre-guard inner sink remains reportable even though the relay call itself is considered guarded by a later guard.
assessment.conditional_mismatch_exits: Covered at tests/test_ipc_multidispatch_guard_matrix.py:76-83. A conditional-only return leaves a mismatch path and retains the candidate; adding an unconditional return suppresses it. relay_guard likewise only counts direct return/throw statements in the mismatch branch's top-level statement list (analysis.py:1855-1865), so a nested conditional return by itself is not treated as an unconditional exit.
assessment.branches: Branch-local guard coverage at tests/test_ipc_multidispatch_guard_matrix.py:72-74 expects the unguarded sibling sink to remain a candidate.
assessment.ambiguous_helper: Overloaded helper coverage at tests/test_ipc_multidispatch_guard_matrix.py:85-97 verifies a nonunique target does not guess a body and leaves one entry finding without claiming Guarded.
assessment.code_test_completeness: No correctness defect observed in the requested cases. Minor test improvement: relay_inner_wrong_then_correct_fixed.cpp:26-30 invokes ReadInterfaceToken() twice, while the multi-dispatch fixture correctly caches one token at line 18 before comparing it. A cached-token relay variant would isolate descriptor identity handling from any cursor/consumption semantics of repeated parcel reads. The current test still exercises the code path and does not invalidate the tested analyzer behavior. A combined committed relay+multi-sink regression would also make the in-memory cross-check permanent; existing unit tests split those dimensions.

limitations: This is an analyzer/unit-fixture review, not validation against OpenHarmony runtime MessageParcel semantics.
Only the two directly relevant test modules were run; no product build or broader suite was run.
reviewer_disposition: Accept current D2/T5 behavior for the requested scenarios; recommend adding a cached-token wrong-then-correct relay fixture and a committed combined relay/multi-sink regression when convenient.
